title: Tomorrow: three meetings, a dentist appointment, and a 4-hour focus block
summary: A plain agenda for one overloaded tomorrow — meetings, dentist, and a protected focus block listed in order.

blocks.title: One day, written as a list
blocks.body: Tomorrow already has three meetings and a dentist appointment. The only way a 4-hour focus block survives is if it appears on the same list with real clock times — not as a hope in the margins.

items.title: Arrive, coffee, open the focus doc
items.detail: Do not check chat yet. Put the focus task title at the top of a note.

items.title: Meeting 1 — standup
items.detail: Camera on if required; decisions only. Park anything that wants to become a second meeting.

items.title: Shallow-work window
items.detail: Chat, email, meeting prep, the small tickets. This is where the interruptions live so the afternoon does not get them.

items.title: Meeting 2 — project sync
items.detail: Bring one status sentence and one ask. Leave with owners, not vibes.

items.title: Lunch and travel buffer
items.detail: Eat something with protein. Leave early enough that parking stress does not eat the focus block.

items.title: Dentist appointment
items.detail: Already booked. Put the confirmation email in a place you can show at the desk.

items.title: Meeting 3 — 1:1
items.detail: Short. If it tries to expand, schedule a follow-up instead of stealing the focus block.

items.title: Focus block — four uninterrupted hours
items.detail: One block, not two halves. Phone face down, chat status: busy, same task start to finish.

items.title: Shutdown
items.detail: Write tomorrow's first line. Close the laptop on purpose.

blocks.title: How the focus block stays real
blocks.body: The only run of the day with nothing booked inside it is 14:50–18:50, so that is the block — one four-hour stretch, not two two-hour halves. The tradeoff is a late finish. If you would rather focus 09:00–13:00, a fixed commitment has to move: make the standup async and slide project sync to the afternoon. What does not work is splitting it — two 2-hour blocks is a different assignment.
